answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a shared reputation score. When an account behaves honestly, its stake is returned; when independent checks confirm fraud, the stake is slashed and the account loses standing. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital for every fabricated identity, not merely mint names. If the onyx market detects a suspicious signal, it can delay payouts until peers test whether the accounts echo one another, making coordinated fakes costly to maintain.
